title: Publish executable protocol specifications and a threat model

events.title: Publish executable protocol specifications and a threat model
events.body:
## Outcome

Make the repository protocol independently implementable with versioned schemas, canonical vectors, a threat model, and a small reference verifier.

## Implementation

- Publish normative specifications for identities and rotation, repository identity and manifests, collaboration and social events, receipts, private envelopes, relay and peer streams, migration, releases, and workflow checks.
- Generate JSON Schemas plus HTTP and WebSocket interface descriptions from one versioned source.
- Document trust boundaries, assets, adversaries, metadata exposure, replay, rollback, equivocation, denial-of-service, key loss, and recovery assumptions.
- Provide positive and negative canonical signing, encryption, fold, transport, and migration vectors.
- Implement a dependency-light reference verifier that validates schemas, signatures, hashes, event folds, manifests, receipts, and stream frames without using production client code.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every sprint object and endpoint has a version, compatibility rule, size bound, and unknown-version behavior.
- Production implementations and the reference verifier agree on every positive vector and reject every negative vector.
- Generated schemas and interface descriptions cannot drift from the normative source.
- The threat model states residual risks and never claims encryption can revoke already decrypted data.
- A clean independent implementation can verify a repository snapshot using only the published artifacts.

## Dependencies

Developed alongside all contract issues; #443 makes the complete specification and verifier a release blocker.

## Verification

Generate all artifacts twice, compare normalized bytes, run every vector in each production implementation and the reference verifier, mutate every signed field, and verify documented version and size failures.
